why:
The quote exists verbatim at sandbox-environments.md:124, and the cited evidence is accurate at the identifier level: sandbox-settings.ts:394 strict-keys the managed `sandbox` block against SANDBOX_SETTING_KEYS (:172-180 — excludedCommands, deniedReadRoots, deniedWriteRoots, additionalWritableRoots, allowUnsandboxedCommands, network, filesystem), and none of the six named keys is in it. The CONSEQUENCE is false — the inert worklist's own recurring false-positive #3 ("the identifier really is unwired while the consequence is false, because something upstream already handled it").

The claim truncates line 124, dropping the third sentence — "See Enforce sandboxing with managed settings for the keys to deploy and how to keep developers from widening the policy" — and then measures us against settings.md's full 30-row key table instead of the enforcement config that section actually specifies. That config is sandboxing.md:400-406: {"sandbox":{"enabled":true,"failIfUnavailable":true,"allowUnsandboxedCommands":false}}, plus "Add excludedCommands", "Add sandbox.credentials entries for credential directories such as ~/.aws and ~/.ssh", and the two lock keys.

Measured against that, key by key:
- allowUnsandboxedCommands:false — SHIPS, deliverable via managed policy, is a floor the user layer cannot unlock (host-sandbox-settings.ts:46-49), wired at SessionManager.ts:3580 and enforced at the spawn: process-supervisor.ts:467-470 throws `process-isolation-unsandboxed-commands-disallowed`.
- excludedCommands — SHIPS, same path (SessionManager.ts:3579, process-supervisor.ts:476-481).
- allowManagedReadPathsOnly / allowManagedDomainsOnly (the "keep developers from widening" half) — both SHIP (SANDBOX_FILESYSTEM_KEYS/SANDBOX_NETWORK_KEYS at :182-183).
- enabled — no key because isolation is not opt-in here. ProcessSupervisor.start calls resolveProcessIsolation unconditionally for every supervised process (process-supervisor.ts:185); the only two bypasses are the two documented keys above (resolveIsolationDowngrade, :463-482). There is no state in which an admin would need to write `enabled: true`.
- failIfUnavailable — no key because there is no warn-and-run-unsandboxed path to suppress. When no backend can express the policy, resolveProcessIsolation THROWS `process-isolation-unavailable:<platform>:<profile>[:<reason>]` with remediation text (isolation-remediation.ts) and the spawn fails. Claude's default is the opposite; the key exists to buy what we do unconditionally.
- credentials — no key, but the protection the doc's advice buys is a built-in unconditional floor: credentialDenyRoots(homedir(), CONFIG_DIR) is seeded into the deny layer at host-sandbox-settings.ts:61-66 and names ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.nessy, ~/.netrc, ~/.gnupg, ~/.kube, browser cookie stores (credential-deny-roots.ts:102-136) — i.e. the exact two dirs the doc tells the admin to add. It is deliberately retained even when filesystem.disabled is set (isolation.ts:56-63, sandbox-settings.ts:798-806), and the code cites Claude's own sandboxing.md:271 "There is no built-in credential deny list" as why it composes its own. On this key we are STRICTER than the documented configuration.
- bwrapPath / socatPath — a written decision already on disk: managed-composition.ts:56-60, "sandbox.bwrapPath and sandbox.socatPath have no counterpart in our schema; there is nothing to compose for them." socatPath configures Claude's sandbox network proxy, which this fork does not have (our network dimension is a boolean egress denial across three backends — isolation.ts denyNetworkEgress).
- autoAllowBashIfSandboxed — a DATED RECORDED DEVIATION, not a defect: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-deviation-unit-5.md:115, category "documented, not implemented", reason "the documented default `true` is conditioned on `sandbox.enabled`, an opt-in Nessy has no analogue of: supervised-process isolation here is unconditional, so porting the default verbatim would auto-approve EVERY Bash command."

Not one of the nine §3 owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md (those are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, listSessionSummaries) — but two of the six keys carry equivalent dated decisions in the plans, and three more are absent because their enforcing state is the fork's unconditional floor.

Residual truth worth keeping, and it is narrower than the row: sandbox.credentials.envVars (deny/mask, injectHosts, allowPlaintextInject) has no analogue — our floor denies credential FILES, not secret environment variables — and that half needs network.tlsTerminate we also lack. That is a specific missing capability, not "the documented enforcement configuration cannot be deployed".
correctedState: The documented enforcement OUTCOME is our unconditional floor, not an undeployable config. Managed delivery of a `sandbox` block exists and is parsed tolerantly (sandbox-settings.ts:378-397). Of the enforcement config sandboxing.md:400-406 actually specifies, `allowUnsandboxedCommands: false` and `excludedCommands` are deliverable and enforced at the spawn (SessionManager.ts:3579-3580 → process-supervisor.ts:467-481), and both managed-lock keys (`filesystem.allowManagedReadPathsOnly`, `network.allowManagedDomainsOnly`) ship. `enabled` and `failIfUnavailable` have no keys because supervised-process isolation is unconditional and fails closed here: resolveProcessIsolation is called for every process (process-supervisor.ts:185) and throws `process-isolation-unavailable:<platform>:<profile>` with remediation rather than falling back to unsandboxed execution — i.e. the state those two keys exist to buy is our default. `credentials` is superseded by a stricter built-in floor (credentialDenyRoots seeded at host-sandbox-settings.ts:61-66; ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.nessy and 15 more, retained even under filesystem.disabled), which Claude explicitly does not ship. `autoAllowBashIfSandboxed` carries a dated "documented, not implemented" decision (deviation-unit-5.md:115), and `bwrapPath`/`socatPath` a written no-counterpart decision (managed-composition.ts:56-60) — socat backs a sandbox network proxy this fork does not have. The one real remaining gap is narrower: `sandbox.credentials.envVars` (deny/mask, injectHosts) and its `network.tlsTerminate` prerequisite are absent, so secret ENV VARS are not stripped or masked for sandboxed commands the way credential files are denied.
